The tool's defaults apply: Wilcoxon rank test with tie correction, `min_cells=30` (skipping cell types with fewer than 30 cells in either arm), `min_pct=0.1`, `lfc=0.25`, `padj=0.05`. Because there is only one library per arm, this is an exploratory ranking, not differential expression: the cell is the unit of the test but not an independent replicate of the condition, so p-values are pseudoreplicated and must not be reported as inferential. Keep genes detected in at least 10% of cells of one of the two groups, apply a Benjamini-Hochberg adjusted p-value cutoff of 0.05 and a minimum absolute log2 fold-change of 0.25, and report which cell types were skipped for having fewer than 30 cells in an arm (expected: Endothelial, HC, Microglia, Pericyte, RGC, RPE).

**Depth-matched ranking check** — Run `run_depth_matched_de` to test whether the DDX41-vs-WT ranking within each cell type is an artefact of the 1.6x greater median sequencing depth in the DDX41 arm. The tool down-samples the deeper arm within each cell type until per-cell UMI distributions match, re-runs the same Wilcoxon contrast, and Spearman-correlates the original ranking against the depth-matched one per direction. A rho >= 0.5 means the ranking is preserved; rho < 0 means the ranking inverts once depth is equalised and must be reported as a detection artefact, not regulation. This is essential before interpreting any pan-cell-type signature, especially ribosomal/translation genes.

**Composition analysis** — Run `run_composition` with `sample_key="sampleid"` and `condition_key="sampleid"` to quantify whether the proportions of the 11 major retinal cell types differ between DDX41 and WT. Because there is only one sample per arm, the tool reports proportions without a statistical test; report the absolute and relative cell counts per cell type per arm (e.g. Rod 4084/5973, BC 801/1708, MG 787/535) as descriptive findings. Flag any population with a large proportional shift as potentially reflecting cell loss or dropout rather than transcriptional change, since pooled scRNA-seq cannot distinguish the two.

**Pathway enrichment per cell type** — Run `run_enrichment` with no `genes` argument so it automatically reads the DE tables written by `run_de` and performs over-representation analysis per cell type, splitting each into up- and down-regulated halves. Test the significant genes (adjusted p < 0.05, |log2FC| > 0.25) against the set of genes actually measured in this experiment (the tested universe), not a generic genome-wide background, and use the GO Biological Process 2023, Reactome 2022, and MSigDB Hallmark 2020 gene-set libraries. Report the top 10 enriched terms per direction per cell type; keep null results for cell types with no enrichment.

**Preranked GSEA per cell type** — Run `run_gsea_prerank` to complement the ORA by walking the complete ranked gene list per cell type (ranked by Wilcoxon z from `run_de`) rather than thresholding a top-N list. This detects coordinated shifts in pathways that no per-gene cutoff would keep, and returns a signed NES (positive = up in DDX41) with FDR and leading-edge genes. Use the same local GO/Reactome/Hallmark gene-set libraries. Do not require agreement with the ORA results — the two use different null hypotheses — and report null results for cell types where nothing passes FDR.

**Cross-cell-type synthesis** — Use `run_code` to read the per-cell-type DE tables and identify genes changed in the same direction across two or more cell types (a shared/pan-retinal signature) versus genes specific to one cell type. Produce a per-cell-type DEG-count summary table (up/down counts per majorclass), volcano plots per cell type, shared up- and down-regulated gene heatmaps, and an enrichment bar plot per cell type. Interpret any same-direction shift across all cell types cautiously, especially ribosomal/translation genes, as potentially technical given the depth imbalance, and cross-check against the depth-matched ranking before calling it biology.
